scenario: RFCS.7a.4: each cascaded withdrawal is recorded before what its own evaluation produces, recursively -- a cause before its consequences at every depth. `make` derives Made from Seed and `ship` derives Shipped from Made, both logically; `watch` is blocked by `no Shipped` and has a join `c.x / c.y > 1.0` over C with y = 0 that has not run. Retracting the Seed ends `make`'s activation, so Made is withdrawn; Made's withdrawal ends `ship`'s, so Shipped is withdrawn; Shipped's withdrawal releases `watch`'s `(g)`, the pair `((g), c1)` is derived for the first time and the all-Int division traps [LEXP.7.15.1]. In cause order the stream reads fact_retract (Seed), fact_retract (Made), fact_retract (Shipped), computation_error. The kinds carry no fact, so the fault is what makes the order visible: a runtime that pushes a buffered cascade retract's record AFTER propagating it gives fact_retract (Seed), computation_error, fact_retract (Shipped), fact_retract (Made), deepest first, which puts the computation_error second. Nothing before the host retract retracts anything, so the stated three are every fact_retract in the run. PATH PINNED: libds's retract bridge at depth >= 2 (wm_rete_bridge.c ds_rete_wm_retract_bridge, the TMS cascade through rete/terminal.c withdraw_justification and ds_engine_retract_rete_fact), whose record takes its buffer slot before it propagates; Mercury's ds.engine retract_unsupported. The lockstep scenario 95_cascade_order (fixture 128_cascade_order) holds the two to each other with fact ids.
rules_ds:
schema Seed scope logical:
    k: String key

schema Made scope logical:
    k: String key

schema Shipped scope logical:
    k: String key

schema G scope logical:
    k: String key

schema C scope logical:
    id: String key
    x: Int mutable
    y: Int mutable

rule make:
    Seed s
->
    emit Made logical k: s.k

rule ship:
    Made m
->
    emit Shipped logical k: m.k

rule watch:
    G g
    no Shipped s where s.k == g.k
    C c where c.x / c.y > 1.0
->
    log info "watch fired"
